record.paper_title: Open Problems Related to Quantum Query Complexity
record.original_question: Does there exist an oracle relative to which QMA differs from QCMA, where QMA is the class of languages whose membership can be proven by a polynomial-size quantum witness state verified in quantum polynomial time, and QCMA is the subclass of QMA where the witness is required to be a classical basis state, i.e. a string?

evidence.quote: Recall that QMA, Quantum Merlin Arthur, is the class of languages L for which membership in L can be proven via a polynomial-size quantum witness state |ϕ⟩ that’s verified in quantum polynomial time. In 2002, Aharonov and Naveh [12] defined QCMA, or Quantum Classical Merlin Arthur, to be the subclass of QMA where the witness |ϕ⟩ =|w⟩ is required to be a classical basis state (i.e., a string).
Problem 1 Is there an oracle relative to which QMA̸= QCMA?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let QMA (Quantum Merlin–Arthur) be the class of languages L for which there exists a polynomial-time quantum verifier V and a polynomial p such that:
- if x ∈ L, then there exists a quantum state |ϕ⟩ on p(|x|) qubits with Pr[V(x,|ϕ⟩) accepts] ≥ 2/3;
- if x ∉ L, then for every quantum state |ϕ⟩ on p(|x|) qubits, Pr[V(x,|ϕ⟩) accepts] ≤ 1/3.

Let QCMA (Quantum Classical Merlin–Arthur) be the subclass of QMA obtained by restricting the witness |ϕ⟩ to be a computational basis state |w⟩ for some classical string w ∈ {0,1}^{p(|x|)}.

For an oracle O, let QMA^O and QCMA^O denote the analogous classes in which the verifier is additionally given query access to O.

Question: Does there exist an oracle O (allowing, in particular, a possibly quantum unitary oracle, or alternatively a classical oracle) such that QMA^O ≠ QCMA^O?
artifact.status_search_result: A quantum-oracle separation between QMA and QCMA was established by Aaronson and Kuperberg (2007). A classical (randomized) oracle separation was subsequently obtained by Natarajan and Nirkhe (arXiv:2210.15380, CCC 2023), using a distribution-testing problem on regular graphs. Thus, the existence of an oracle making QMA ≠ QCMA is established in both the quantum-oracle and classical-oracle settings.

status_evidence.title: A distribution testing oracle separation between QMA and QCMA
status_evidence.snippet: We construct a randomized classical oracle separating QMA from QCMA.
status_evidence.claim: A classical oracle separation between QMA and QCMA was achieved by Natarajan and Nirkhe.

status_evidence.title: A Distribution Testing Oracle Separating QMA and QCMA (CCC 2023)
status_evidence.snippet: Published version of the classical-oracle separation between QMA and QCMA.
status_evidence.claim: The result appeared in CCC 2023, providing a classical oracle separation.
